ai_show_review.summary: Dark Star & The Eleven dominate a mixed-quality set
ai_show_review.blurb: The second half erupts with a soaring Dark Star, tight The Eleven, and an exuberant Turn On Your Lovelight. Garcia’s tone is vibrant and his solos cut through despite early technical hiccups. Overall the show is worth listening for the high‑energy jams.
ai_show_review.review: May 10, 1969 – Rose Palace in Pasadena was a night of contrast. The first half suffered from power cutouts and a string of filler material that never quite found its footing, but once the band launched into Dark Star the performance lifted off. Garcia’s guitar roared with a bright, over‑driven tone, weaving through an expansive improvisation that stayed compelling even when the tape hiss threatened to intrude. The momentum carried straight into Saint Stephen and then The Eleven, where the rhythm section locked into a hypnotic 11/8 groove, showcasing Mickey Hart’s subtle accents and Bill Kreutzmann’s steady drive. The set closed with an electrifying Turn On Your Lovelight, highlighted by Pigpen’s organ textures that nudged Jerry into fresh melodic territory. While one soundboard source is marred by mid‑set digi‑noise, the overall musical flow—especially the second‑half jams—makes this show a solid addition to any Deadhead’s collection.

best_recording.reason: Good soundboard mix with clear capture of the second‑half jams; despite early filler, it delivers the best overall listening experience.

key_highlights: Spectacular Dark Star improvisation despite tape noise
The Eleven’s tight, rhythmic drive in 11/8 time
Turn On Your Lovelight climax with vibrant organ textures
Garcia’s bright tone and powerful solos cut through technical hiccups

band_performance.Jerry: Garcia’s tone is praised – amp turned up loud, vibrant voice, and powerful soloing especially on Dark Star and Turn On Your Lovelight; even when masked by digi‑noise his improvisational flow still shines.
